acts.4.p1.b1.text: While Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple guard and the Sadducees came up to them,

acts.4.p1.b2.text: greatly disturbed that they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead.

acts.4.p1.b3.text: They seized Peter and John, and because it was evening, they put them in custody until the next day.

acts.4.p2.b1.text: But many who heard the message believed, and the number of men grew to about five thousand.

acts.4.p2.b2.text: The next day the rulers, elders, and scribes assembled in Jerusalem,

acts.4.p2.b3.text: along with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and many others from the high priest’s family.

acts.4.p2.b4.text: “By what power or what name did you do this?”

acts.4.p3.b1.text: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “Rulers and elders of the people!

acts.4.p3.b3.text: … It is by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified but whom God raised from the dead, that this man stands before you healed.

acts.4.p4.b1.text: This Jesus is ‘the stone you builders rejected, …

acts.4.p4.b3.text: Salvation exists in no one else, …

acts.4.p4.b4.text: … for there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved.”

acts.4.p5.b1.text: When they saw the boldness of Peter and John and realized that they were unschooled, ordinary men, they marveled …

acts.4.p5.b2.text: … and took note that these men had been with Jesus.

acts.4.p5.b3.text: And seeing the man who had been healed standing there with them, …

acts.4.p5.b4.text: … they had nothing to say in response.

acts.4.p6.b1.text: So they ordered them to leave the Sanhedrin and then conferred together.

acts.4.p6.b2.text: “What shall we do with these men?” … “It is clear to everyone living in Jerusalem that a remarkable miracle has occurred through them, and we cannot deny it.

acts.4.p6.b3.text: … we must warn them not to speak to anyone in this name.”

acts.4.p7.b1.text: Then they called them in again and commanded them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.

acts.4.p7.b2.text: “Judge for yourselves whether it is right in God’s sight to listen to you rather than God.

acts.4.p7.b3.text: For we cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard.”

acts.4.p8.b1.text: After further threats they let them go. They could not find a way to punish them, …

acts.4.p8.b2.text: … because all the people were glorifying God for what had happened.

acts.4.p8.b3.text: For the man who was miraculously healed was over forty years old.

acts.4.p9.b1.text: On their release, Peter and John returned to their own people and reported everything that the chief priests and elders had said to them.

acts.4.p9.b2.text: “Sovereign Lord,” … “You made the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them.

acts.4.p9.b3.text: ‘Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?

acts.4.p9.b4.text: The kings of the earth take their stand and the rulers gather together against the Lord and against His Anointed One.’

acts.4.p10.b1.text: In fact, this is the very city where Herod and Pontius Pilate conspired with the Gentiles and the people of Israel against Your holy servant Jesus, whom You anointed.

acts.4.p10.b2.text: And now, Lord, consider their threats, and enable Your servants to speak Your word with complete boldness,

acts.4.p10.b3.text: as You stretch out Your hand to heal and perform signs and wonders through the name of Your holy servant Jesus.”

acts.4.p11.b1.text: After they had prayed, their meeting place was shaken, …

acts.4.p11.b2.text: … and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit …

acts.4.p11.b3.text: … and spoke the word of God boldly.

acts.4.p12.b1.text: The multitude of believers was one in heart and soul. No one claimed that any of his possessions was his own, but they shared everything they owned.

acts.4.p12.b2.text: With great power the apostles continued to give their testimony about the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And abundant grace was upon them all.

acts.4.p12.b3.text: … those who owned lands or houses would sell their property, bring the proceeds from the sales,

acts.4.p12.b4.text: and lay them at the apostles’ feet for distribution to anyone as he had need.

acts.4.p13.b2.text: … whom the apostles called Barnabas (meaning Son of Encouragement),

acts.4.p13.b3.text: sold a field he owned, brought the money, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
